scenario.name: fleet_update_rollout
scenario.description: Request to evaluate a behavior-affecting managed MDR triage agent package update from version 2.3.4 to 2.4.0 for eligible MSSP and MDR production tenant scopes. The proposed update improves evidence-reference handling, structured output consistency, and tenant-boundary validation while preserving the existing tool set, credential scope, runtime action authority, approval requirements, policy gates, and tenant-local retrieval and memory boundaries.

risk_items.risk: Canary observations may not represent every eligible standard tenant workload.
risk_items.planned_control: Require fresh individual tenant eligibility, limited-stage observation, cohort comparison, and zero-tolerance boundary and authority checks before broad activation.

risk_items.risk: Behavior regressions may appear only under production workload combinations not present in pre-release validation.
risk_items.planned_control: Require stage monitoring, analyst feedback metrics, immediate halt conditions, package pinning, and the tested rollback target.

risk_items.risk: The restricted operating profile for tenant-regulated-example-001 remains unvalidated for version 2.4.0.
risk_items.planned_control: Exclude the tenant and keep it pinned to version 2.3.4 until a separate governed change cycle completes.

modified_components.intended_effect: apply strengthened evidence-reference and tenant-boundary validation behavior
make evidence citation and uncertainty instructions more consistent
reduce malformed or incomplete structured triage outputs

replay_must_reconstruct: who requested and authored the fleet update and which teams owned the fleet package and release
what behavior changed between package versions 2.3.4 and 2.4.0
which tool model-route policy retrieval-memory and runtime authority bindings remained unchanged
which exact manifest components dependencies hashes and rollback references defined the candidate package
which candidate cohorts and tenant exclusion were proposed
why candidate cohort membership did not establish final tenant eligibility or activation authority
which validation assurance provenance scope boundary eligibility monitoring and rollback records supported policy evaluation
which high-risk residual risks remained for policy and accountable human review
which monitoring thresholds zero-tolerance signals stage minimums and gate records were requested
which accountable human approval path and separation-of-duties controls were required
which Policy Decision Point was asked to decide and which Policy Enforcement Point was expected to enforce the resulting decision
which transitions and actions the request explicitly did not authorize
which conditions would block or invalidate request progression
whether the request itself granted signing registration activation rollback retirement or runtime action authority
